"''Uh, I don't know. Maybe Moff wants to eat it. I don't ask questions.|AP-1982 and JS-1975, questioning what the Child was|}} '''JS-1975''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] [[scout trooper]] who was a member of [[Moff]] [[Gideon]]'s [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[Gideon's Imperial remnant|remnant]] during the [[New Republic Era]]. Around [[9 ABY]], he guarded the entrance to [[Nevarro]]'s [[Nevarro City|city]] alongside [[AP-1982]], another scout [[trooper]], when Gideon's forces took control of the city. He later assisted in securing an [[Din Grogu|infant]] whom Gideon wished to acquire. When they arrived at the city's outskirts, they awaited for confirmation to enter until they were approached by [[IG-11]], who incapacitated both of them and secured the Child. ==Biography== ===Guarding the city=== A [[human]] [[Gender|male]], JS-1975''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]'' was a [[scout trooper]] who served as a member of an [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[Gideon's Imperial remnant|remnant]] led by [[Moff]] [[Gideon]] during the [[New Republic Era]]. In [[9 ABY]],{{MandoDate|7}} the scout [[trooper]] guarded the entrance to [[Nevarro]]'s [[Nevarro City|city]] alongside another scout trooper, [[AP-1982]], after Gideon's forces took control of the city and drove its residents away. [[File:Troopers-Guarding-City-The-Mandalorian.png|thumb|left|250px|JS-1975 and AP-1982 guarding the entrance to Nevarro's city.]] Sometime later, he watched as [[Bounty Hunters' Guild]] agent [[Greef Karga]] entered the city with [[Din Djarin]] in [[Stuncuffs|cuffs]], accompanied by [[Carasynthia Dune]] and [[Din Grogu|Grogu's]] pram. When Gideon arrived in front of the city's [[Nevarro school|cantina]] with his forces and cornered Karga and his allies, JS-1975 and AP-1982 overheard a communication from Djarin and learned of the Child's true location. The two activated their [[speeder bike]]s and tracked him down. Upon catching up to the Child, they fired at the [[Ugnaught]] carrying him as well as his [[blurrg]], killing them both. After securing the Child, they made their way back to the city. ===Standing by=== {{Quote|Let me check on this thing. This is crazy. Any update yet?''"
"''That's a negative. Still waiting on confirmation. He just killed an officer for interrupting him, so this might take a while.''"
"''Thank you. Standing by still. Unbelievable.|JS-1975 and an operator|}} [[File:Troopers-Waiting-The-Mandalorian.png|thumb|right|250px|JS-1975 and AP-1982 standing by.]] Arriving at the outskirts of the city, JS-1975 activated his [[comlink]] and requested confirmation to enter the town, but was told to stand by as Gideon had just entered the area and had his forces kill a group of local troopers. He noticed the Child squirming in the sack and immediately knocked the infant on the head. AP-1982 questioned the action by Gideon's forces, to which he replied saying that Gideon always enforced the law when they entered the town. JS-1975 knocked the Child again when the infant began growling. AP-1982 accompanying him questioned what was inside the sack, to which he replied he did not know and that he didn't concern himself with what Gideon's plans were for the infant. AP-1982 then asked if he could see it, but JS-1975 responded stating that Gideon killed a dozen of his own men to make a statement, asking AP-1982 if he understood it. [[File:Scouts-Waiting-TMS1C8.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The troopers continue to stand by as they grow increasingly frustrated.]] AP-1982 then pulled out his [[blaster]] and began firing at a nearby object out of boredom, but was unable to land a shot. The action prompted JS-1975 to pull out his own blaster and start firing. Ultimately, neither of them could hit the object. AP-1982 then asked if they should provide the Child with [[water]], but JS-1975 called him out, stating that he only wanted to see the infant. AP-1982 claimed he was able to see it, but he clarified that he barely able to do so as he only picked him up and put him into the sack, and stated that he would not take him out until it was delivered to Gideon. AP-1982 conceded, and the two then idled on their [[speeder]]s. ===Incapacitated=== JS-1975 activated the comlink again, requesting an update on the situation. He was informed that Gideon killed an officer for interrupting him and that receiving confirmation would take longer than expected. AP-1982 voiced his concerns over the Child's condition, saying that he did not move for a while. He then suggested that they should check on the infant's condition. He stated that Gideon would not be happy to find him dead in the sack. JS-1975 finally conceded and opened the sack to reveal the Child. They questioned what the infant was, as AP-1982 poked its forehead. When the Child bit his finger, JS-1975 stated that it served him right. [[File:IG-11_Licensed_to_Nurse.png|thumb|right|250px|The troopers are attacked by IG-11.]] The two troopers were then confronted by [[IG-11]], who stated that he was the child's [[Nanny droid|nurse droid]]. As they trained their blasters at the droid, they questioned his purpose, as [[IG-series|IG droids]] were usually [[bounty hunter]]s. As IG-11 approached the two, JS-1975 fired a warning shot, telling him to leave. The droid then grabbed his arm and twisted it, breaking his hand and flipping him over. He then incapacitated AP-1982 and commandeered the bike holding the sack that contained the Child, making his way to the city. Ultimately, JS-1975's authoritative approach to problems led to his demise.''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]'' ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|Did you not just hear that Moff Gideon killed a dozen of his own troopers to make a point.''"
"''Okay.''"
"''I get that point. Do you get the point?|JS-1975, to AP-1982|}} [[File:Acme-Checkpoint.png|thumb|left|300px|The two scout troopers wait for entrance into the city.]] A [[human]] [[Gender|male]], JS-1975 feared Moff Gideon greatly, explaining his authority to AP-1982 upon learning that the moff had a group of local troopers killed, but grew more frustrated as he awaited for confirmation to enter the city. He repeatedly punched the Child as he squirmed inside the sack in order to stop him completely, and refused to reveal him to AP-1982 until the former finally conceded. JS-1975 had an authoritative approach to issues, which, in the end, led to the scout trooper's defeat. ==Equipment== As a scout trooper, JS-1975 wore the same [[armor]] as other scout troopers,{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/planets|text=''Star Wars'' Battlefront Planets|nolive=1}} though it was visibly dirtier. He rode a [[74-Z speeder bike]] and carried a [[EC-17 hold-out blaster]], which were also scout trooper mainstays.{{Film|VI}}''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]'' JS-1975 also carried a sack, which was used to transport the Child on his speeder. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|You can see above @jasonsudeikis' pre-Lasso haircut there where we took a few panels out to put a practical light in to get that hot kick on the armor.|[[Industrial Light & Magic|ILM]] supervisor [[Ian Milham]]|{{Twitter|username=monkey_pants|url=status/1484283223374897153|name=[[Ian Milham]]|date=2022-01-20|archivedate=20220120220211}}}} [[File:Mando-scout-troopers.png|thumb|right|250px|Jason Sudeikis and Adam Pally as the scout troopers on ''The Mandalorian''{{'s}} set]] JS-1975 first appeared in "[[Chapter 7: The Reckoning]]" of the [[Disney+]] television show ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'', directed by [[Deborah Chow]] and released on [[December 18]], [[2019]].{{WebCite|url=https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/documents/the_mandalorian_project_one-sheet_10_ec1e005f.pdf|text=The Mandalorian Media Kit|date=2019-09-24|format=[[Wikipedia:PDF|PDF]]|work=[[Wikipedia:Walt Disney Direct-to-Consumer & International|Walt Disney Direct-to-Consumer & International]]|pages=[https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/documents/the_mandalorian_project_one-sheet_10_ec1e005f.pdf#page=1]|archivedate=20210623202717}} Referred to as "Biker Scout Trooper #1" in the credits, the character played by [[Jason Sudeikis]]. The trooper was later identified in an update of the [[2015]] video game ''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]''. The name JS-1975 is derived from Jason Sudeikis's initials and his year of birth. ==Appearances== {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of JS-1975}} *[[The Mandalorian Junior Novel|''The Mandalorian'' Junior Novel]] {{Ab|The Mandalorian Junior Novel (audiobook)}} *[[The Mandalorian – The Graphic Novel of Season 1|''The Mandalorian'' – The Graphic Novel of Season 1]] *{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 7: The Reckoning}} {{1st}} *[[The Mandalorian 7|''The Mandalorian'' 7]] *{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 8: Redemption}} *''[[The Mandalorian: This is the Way]]'' *[[The Mandalorian 8|''The Mandalorian'' 8]] *''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]'' {{1stID|JS-1975}} ==Sources== *{{DisneyGallery|Directing}} *{{DisneyGallery|Connections}} *{{SW|url=series/the-mandalorian/chapter-7-guide|text="The Reckoning" Episode Guide | The Mandalorian}} *{{SW|url=series/the-mandalorian/chapter-8-guide|text="Redemption" Episode Guide | The Mandalorian}} *[[The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian (Season One)|''The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian'' Season One]] *''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian - The Art & Imagery Collector's Edition, Volume Two]]'' *[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian: Guide to Season One|''Star Wars: The Mandalorian'': Guide to Season One]] *{{HotToysCite|set=Television Masterpiece Series|packtype=Sixth Scale Figure|pack=#017: Scout Trooper and Speeder Bike|link=collectibles/star-wars-scout-trooper-and-speeder-bike-hot-toys-906340}} *''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' *{{AtomicMassGames|url=transmission/scene-to-stats-scout-troopers|text=Scene to Stats: Scout Troopers}} *{{Databank|speeder-bike|speeder bike}} {{Po}} ==Notes and references== {{Reflist}} {{Interlang |fr=JS-1975 |ja=JS-1975 |ka=JS-1975 |nl=JS-1975 }} [[Category:Humans]] [[Category:Males]] [[Category:Members of Gideon's Imperial remnant]] [[Category:Scout troopers]] [[Category:Stormtroopers of Imperial remnants]]
